200.q: I fill with water, tumble your clothes in circles, and buzz when the load is finished. What am I?
I roar across the carpet and swallow crumbs into a bag or a canister. What am I?
I glide across shirts on a padded board and hiss steam to flatten the wrinkles. What am I?
I blow hot air at your head so you can leave the bathroom without dripping. What am I?
I have no buttons and no sleeves, yet I am pulled over you at night to trap your own warmth. What am I?
I clamp over your ears so the music belongs to you alone. What am I?
I vanish into the sofa cushions, and without me nobody can change the channel. What am I?
I have a lens and a shutter, and I trap a single moment with one click. What am I?
I pinch the laundry to the line so the wind cannot steal it. What am I?
My tip is flat or crossed, and I sink threaded metal into wood without a single blow. What am I?
I cover the whole floor, soften every footstep, and hide the dust underneath me. What am I?
I arrive in a flat cardboard box, I am cut into triangles, and everyone argues over my last piece. What am I?
I am fried, glazed, and famous for the emptiness in my middle. What am I?
I am a crisp cup you are allowed to eat, and I hold something cold until it drips down your wrist. What am I?
I arrive in a thousand pieces and I am only finished when the last one clicks into place. What am I?
I ride on both your shoulders and carry your books to class. What am I?
I have wheels and a pull handle, and I trail behind you through the airport. What am I?
I have four small wheels under a wooden plank, and I roll away the moment you step off. What am I?
I buckle under your chin and I take the blow so your skull does not. What am I?
I have spinning blades in a jug, and I turn whole fruit into a drink in seconds. What am I?
I sit folded on your lap through dinner and wipe your mouth between bites. What am I?
I am a thin tube that lets you drink without ever lifting the glass. What am I?
I hang from a high ceiling, dripping with glass, and I light a grand room from above. What am I?
I have a slot in my back, coins rattle inside me, and children shake me to guess how full I am. What am I?
I have curved runners instead of flat feet, so I tip back and forth while going nowhere. What am I?
I stand in the kitchen corner with a bag inside me, and I go out to the street once a week. What am I?
You twist wood into me and thin curled shavings fall out the other side. What am I?
I spin on a tilted stand, and every country in the world sits on my surface. What am I?
I am a long tube of lenses, and I bring distant worlds close to a single eye. What am I?
I lie coiled beside the house, and when the tap turns I carry a drink to the flowers. What am I?
I growl across the lawn and leave neat pale stripes behind me. What am I?
I have a broad blade and a long shaft, and I move earth one scoop at a time. What am I?
I am slung between two trees, and I rock you to sleep in the shade. What am I?
I have a line, a reel, and a hook, and I wait patiently at the water's edge. What am I?
I have three valves and a flared brass mouth, and I only sound when your lips buzz. What am I?
I am carved with a grinning face, lit from inside, and I glow on porches every October. What am I?
I wear one small flame for every year you have lived, and I am cut once the singing stops. What am I?
I am printed overnight and folded onto the doorstep, and by tomorrow I am worth nothing. What am I?
I am a stick of wax in a paper wrapper, and I come in a box of many colours. What am I?
I am yellow, I swing an arm out at every stop, and all traffic must halt when my red lights flash. What am I?

400.q: I hang on a cord around a referee's neck, and one sharp breath from me stops the whole game. What am I?
I am a staircase that never stops moving, so standing still on me still gets you there. What am I?
I turn in a circle so people can come and go at once without ever letting the weather in. What am I?
I rise because what is inside me is warmer than what is outside, and I carry a wicker basket beneath. What am I?
I have no wings at all, yet I can hang motionless in the sky and land where no runway exists. What am I?
I have huge rear wheels and small front ones, and I drag a plough across the field. What am I?
I throw water into the air only to catch it again, and strangers toss coins into me for luck. What am I?
I have a mantel above me and a grate below, and I warm the room while sending my breath up the flue. What am I?
I am white, soft and sugary, and I turn golden and gooey on the end of a stick. What am I?
I am poured as batter, flipped in a pan, and stacked with syrup on top. What am I?
I am two metal leaves joined by a pin, and without me a door would only be a board. What am I?
I am wide at one end and narrow at the other, and I stop the liquid escaping as it is poured. What am I?
I am a grooved wheel, and a rope across me turns a downward pull into an upward lift. What am I?
I have a bubble trapped in liquid, and builders trust me to say when something is perfectly flat. What am I?
I grip a nut or a bolt and lend your hand the leverage to turn it. What am I?
I sit on a fingertip so the blunt end of a needle can be pushed without pain. What am I?
I am a tube with a mirror at each end, and I let a hidden watcher see over the top. What am I?
I perch on a rooftop, often shaped like a rooster, and I turn to show where the breeze is coming from. What am I?
Turn me and the coloured chips inside fall into a brand new symmetrical pattern every time. What am I?
I swing back and forth, and only my length decides how long each swing takes. What am I?
I sit on the wall, feel how warm the room is, and tell the heating when to start and stop. What am I?
I live on the ceiling, I chirp when my power runs low, and burnt toast sets me screaming. What am I?
I lock solid when you yank me hard, but let go gently if you pull me slowly. What am I?
I am folded away out of sight and I inflate in a fraction of a second when metal meets metal. What am I?
I am a ridge laid across the road that slows you by threatening your suspension. What am I?
I am a silk case a caterpillar spins around itself, and something with wings breaks out of me. What am I?
I happen when the moon slides directly between you and the star we orbit, and staring at me can blind you. What am I?
I am a spinning column reaching from cloud to ground, and I can lift a roof clean off a house. What am I?
I am tonnes of loose snow that a single loud shout can send down a mountainside. What am I?
I look like solid ground until you step on me, and struggling only pulls you deeper. What am I?
I am a spinning pit of water that drags anything floating toward my centre. What am I?
I am barely a ripple in deep ocean but a wall of water at the shore, and an undersea quake usually starts me. What am I?
I make the invisible visible by looking down through my lenses rather than up. What am I?
I am a wedge of glass that takes one white beam and spreads it into a band of colours. What am I?
Thrown correctly, I do the one thing no other thrown object does: I return to the hand that released me. What am I?
I am a grid of black and white squares, and my clues are numbered across and down. What am I?
I have six coloured faces and fifty-four squares, and twisting me is far easier than fixing me. What am I?
I glow in the corner of a diner; feed me a coin and choose the record I will play. What am I?
I have flippers, bumpers and a spring-loaded plunger, and shoving me too hard ends your turn. What am I?
I count upward from zero at the press of a thumb, and coaches at the trackside live by me. What am I?

600.q: Rearrange every one of my letters and you get an entirely different word; that shuffle is all I am. What am I?
I am a pronounceable new word built from the first letters of a longer phrase. What am I?
I set two words side by side that flatly contradict each other, like a deafening hush. What am I?
When the jar was opened and every evil flew out into the world, I alone stayed behind. What am I?
I hold you to the ground and keep the moon in its orbit, yet I am the feeblest of nature's four forces. What am I?
I steal the speed from a rolling ball and I am also the reason your shoes grip the floor. What am I?
I am the measure of disorder, and in a closed system I only ever increase. What am I?
I am why a standing passenger lurches forward the instant the brakes slam on. What am I?
I lift water into the sky without ever boiling it, and I am why a puddle disappears on a warm day. What am I?
I am the water that appears on the outside of a cold glass, though none of it came from within. What am I?
I carve canyons with nothing but water, wind and patience. What am I?
I turn up once every four years to keep the calendar honest, though some century marks skip me. What am I?
I am the longest circle drawn around the globe, and nothing marks me on the ground below. What am I?
I am the light that lingers once the sun has gone but before real darkness arrives. What am I?
Not even light can climb back out of me, and my edge is a boundary of no return. What am I?
I am no star at all, only a speck of dust burning up in the air, yet people make wishes on me. What am I?
I rise from a cave floor drip by drip, reaching upward toward my hanging twin. What am I?
I am tree resin hardened over millions of years, and insects sometimes lie perfectly preserved inside me. What am I?
I am the gentle phrase people reach for when the honest word feels too blunt. What am I?
I am a phrase whose meaning has nothing to do with the words in it, such as kicking the bucket. What am I?
I was a fresh and striking phrase once, and endless repetition wore me out. What am I?
I carry the blame for a whole group's failure, and I am named for an animal driven into the wilderness. What am I?
Nobody expects me to win, which is exactly why the crowd roars when I do. What am I?
In chess I am the draw that comes when a player has no legal move yet is not in check. What am I?
I am an opening in which a player deliberately gives up material to gain a better position. What am I?
I am the blank expression worn at the card table so that nothing at all is given away. What am I?
I am handed down through generations, and my worth is counted in memory rather than money. What am I?
I am a statement that seems to contradict itself and may still turn out to be true. What am I?
I hide my answer in plain sight and then dare you to name me. What am I?
I am your outline filled in solid black, showing your shape but none of your features. What am I?
I am a picture assembled from broken fragments, and I only make sense from a distance. What am I?
I am the invented name an author signs so the real one stays hidden. What am I?
I exist when one seller is the only seller, and buyers have nowhere else to go. What am I?
I am the price of borrowing money, and left long enough I begin to grow on myself. What am I?
Economists commonly declare me when output shrinks for two quarters in a row. What am I?
I burn myself to ash and rise out of it again, over and over, in the old myths. What am I?
I keep you staring at the ceiling long after the rest of the house has gone quiet. What am I?
I strike the moment the curtain rises, and I steal lines you knew perfectly an hour earlier. What am I?
I am the sudden flash of understanding that makes a person leap up and shout aloud. What am I?
I am the speech of praise delivered about someone who can no longer hear a word of it. What am I?
